findings.title: Disable bytecode output before importing the actual bound method
findings.evidence: The harness load_bound_runner and both generated wrappers use SourceFileLoader to import the actual method path. Neither sets sys.dont_write_bytecode before import; wrapper Popen calls inherit the caller environment. The manifest PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE setting applies only later to commands launched by the runner.
findings.failure_trace: With normal Python bytecode caching enabled, imports can create __pycache__ beside the actual task method, outside the controlled synthetic roots and their size accounting. This violates the fixture's declared write containment even though source bytes remain unchanged.
findings.required_change: Set sys.dont_write_bytecode=True in the harness and both generated wrappers before any bound-method import, or explicitly enforce an equivalent environment/-B requirement for all of those processes.

accepted_design_properties: The controlled synthetic-root design itself is valid for Python-only lifecycle logic, with separate actual-root accounting evidence retained.
Both wrappers bind the exact accepted R3 source hash, import that source with SourceFileLoader and override only R/S/D before main.
Manifest runner_sha256 binds original SOURCE rather than wrapper bytes, while pre/post readsets protect both source and wrappers.
Production signal handlers, fixed resource predicates/caps, prefix/ownership checks and deliberate finalization digest fault injection remain.
Scope labels distinguish synthetic-root lifecycle/finalization from full-root execution.
preserved_failures: Prior full-root lifecycle timeout and incomplete full old/new scanner fixture remain failed/incomplete; no clock, cap or success history is reset.
